version: RBI/DOR/2025-26/363 DOR.ORG.REC.No.282/21-04-158/2025-26 dated 28.11.2025 (NBFCs; ids follow this text); CB 171, SFB 202, PB 220, LAB 245, UCB 293, RCB 318, AIFI 337, CIC 379

groups.title: Chapter I - Preliminary: A. Short Title and Commencement

controls.title: Existing IT outsourcing agreements comply by 10 April 2026 or at renewal; new agreements from signature
controls.prose: The Directions come into force with immediate effect (28 November 2025). Existing IT outsourcing agreements, whether or not they are due for renewal on or after that date, must comply with the Directions either at renewal or by 10 April 2026, whichever is earlier; new IT outsourcing agreements that come into force on or after the effective date must comply from the date of the agreement itself. The proviso does not permit non-compliance with any other extant regulatory instruction or statutory requirement.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx compares contract.startDate and the renewal date in company-profile/<c>/vendors/<vendor_id>.json with 2025-11-28 and 2026-04-10: an IT agreement signed on or after 28 Nov 2025, or any existing material IT agreement after 10 Apr 2026, that lacks the paragraph 74 clause set is a finding against the missing clause control. Financial-services outsourcing (Chapter III) has no transition window. The RCB Directions have no IT chapter and no such proviso. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 2; UCB 2; RCB 2; LAB/AIFI/CIC 2.
evidenceExpected: Register of IT outsourcing agreements with start and renewal dates
Remediation plan or amended contracts for agreements pre-dating 28 Nov 2025

params.label: Date by which existing IT outsourcing agreements must comply, if not renewed earlier

groups.title: Chapter I - Preliminary: B. Applicability and Scope

controls.title: Determine which chapters bind the entity by entity class and NBFC layer
controls.prose: The NBFC Directions apply to NBFC-D, NBFC-ICC, NBFC-Factor, NBFC-MFI, NBFC-IFC, IDF-NBFC, HFCs, SPDs, CICs (Core Investment Companies), NBFC-P2P and NBFC-AA, subject to layer-wise applicability: NBFCs in the Base Layer are bound by everything except Chapter IV (IT services) and the IT-specific provisions of Chapter II; NBFCs in the Middle Layer and above are bound by the whole Directions, including Chapter IV; Mortgage Guarantee Companies in the Middle Layer and above are bound by Chapter IV and the IT-specific paragraphs of Chapter II; the Directions do not apply to NOFHCs.
controls.guidance: refresh-ctx reads details.json entityTypes and regulatoryRegistrations[].category and records which chapters apply. The sibling Directions scope differently: Commercial Banks (Scheduled Commercial Banks, para 3), SFBs and Payments Banks (para 3) take Chapters III and IV; Urban Co-operative Banks (para 3) take Chapter III and the non-IT parts of Chapter II for every tier but Chapter IV only for Tier-3 and Tier-4; Rural Co-operative Banks (State and Central Co-operative Banks, para 3) have a financial-services chapter only; Local Area Banks, All India Financial Institutions (EXIM Bank, NABARD, NaBFID, NHB, SIDBI) and Credit Information Companies (para 3) have an IT-services chapter only. Local Area Banks and Rural Co-operative Banks have no slug in vocab/entity-types, so Maxwell cannot select this catalog for them until the vocab gains one. CICs in the NBFC Directions are Core Investment Companies (entity type nbfc), not Credit Information Companies. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 3; UCB 3; RCB 3; LAB/AIFI/CIC 3.
evidenceExpected: details.json entityTypes and NBFC layer / UCB tier registration
Applicability memo naming the chapters that bind the entity

controls.title: Foreign bank branches: Head Office reads as Board; comply-or-explain for IT outsourcing
controls.prose: For foreign banks operating in India in branch mode, any reference to the Board or Board of Directors is read as a reference to the Head Office or Controlling Office that oversees the Indian branch operations; for Chapter IV (outsourcing of IT services) foreign banks follow a comply-or-explain approach and may deviate from a specific provision subject to examination and acceptance by RBI of a reasonably justifiable explanation.
controls.guidance: Evidence the Head Office or Controlling Office approvals used in place of Board approvals, and a register of Chapter IV deviations with the explanation submitted to RBI and RBI acceptance. A deviation without an accepted explanation is a finding against the underlying Chapter IV control. Commercial Banks Directions para 3 only; no equivalent in the other eight entity-wise Directions.
evidenceExpected: Head Office / Controlling Office approval records
Register of Chapter IV deviations with RBI acceptance

controls.title: UCBs: Chapter IV and IT-specific Board duties bind only Tier-3 and Tier-4 banks
controls.prose: The UCB Directions apply to all Urban Co-operative Banks (Primary Co-operative Banks under section 5(ccv) read with section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949); Chapter IV and the IT-specific provisions of Chapter II (such as the Board-level IT outsourcing policy and Board reviews of IT outsourcing) apply only to Tier-3 and Tier-4 UCBs as classified under the RBI UCB Licensing, Scheduling and Regulatory Classification Guidelines, 2025, while the remaining provisions of Chapter II apply to all UCBs including Tier-1 and Tier-2.
controls.guidance: refresh-ctx records the UCB tier from regulatoryRegistrations[].category (tier-1..tier-4); the IT controls of this catalog carry reCategories tier-3 and tier-4 for that reason. UCB Directions para 3 only.
evidenceExpected: UCB tier classification recorded in details.json

controls.title: Scope of Chapter III: outsourcing of financial services
controls.prose: Chapter III applies to material outsourcing arrangements that the NBFC enters into with a service provider, whether a member of its group or conglomerate or an unrelated party, located in India or elsewhere, for financial services such as applications processing (loan origination, credit card), document processing, marketing and research, supervision of loans, data processing and back-office activities; for outsourced credit card services the NBFC Credit Cards: Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2025 also apply. It does not apply to IT services (defined in paragraph 58(1)) unless Chapter IV says so, nor to activities unrelated to financial services such as courier, staff catering, housekeeping and janitorial services, premises security, and movement and archiving of records.
controls.guidance: Classify each vendor service in company-profile/<c>/vendors/<vendor_id>.json as Chapter III (financial service), Chapter IV (IT service) or out of scope. For NBFCs only material arrangements are in Chapter III scope; the bank Directions (CB, SFB, PB, UCB, RCB para 4) apply Chapter III to all outsourcing arrangements, and the Commercial Bank and Payments Bank texts also exclude audit assignments to Chartered Accountant firms (para 4(3)). Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 4; UCB 4; RCB 4-5; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Classification of every outsourcing arrangement into Chapter III, Chapter IV or out of scope

controls.title: Banks: sub-contracted financial services are in scope and need prior consent after review
controls.prose: Chapter III applies, mutatis mutandis, to sub-contracted activities: the outsourcing contract must provide for prior approval or consent of the bank before the service provider engages any sub-contractor for all or part of the outsourced activity, and before granting consent the bank must review the sub-contracting arrangement and ensure it complies with Chapter III.
controls.guidance: For every Chapter III vendor with contract.subcontractingAllowed true, obtain the consent record and the bank review that preceded it for each entry in services[].subcontractors. A sub-contractor listed without a consent and review record is a high finding. CB, SFB and PB Directions para 4(2); the UCB and RCB Directions place the same review-before-consent duty in agreement clause 30(iv); the NBFC text requires only prior approval (34(iv)).
evidenceExpected: Contract clause requiring prior consent for sub-contracting
Consent and pre-consent review record per sub-contractor

controls.title: Scope of Chapter IV: material outsourcing of IT services and the listed exclusions
controls.prose: Chapter IV applies to material outsourcing of IT services, including IT infrastructure management, maintenance and support; network and security solutions and maintenance; application development, maintenance and testing by Application Service Providers including ATM Switch ASPs; data centre services and operations; cloud computing services; managed security services; and management of IT infrastructure and technology services associated with the payment system ecosystem. It does not apply to corporate internet banking obtained from another RE; external audit services such as VA/PT, IS audit and security review; SMS gateways; procurement of IT hardware or appliances; acquisition of licensed or subscribed software and vendor enhancements to it; OEM maintenance including security patches and bug fixes; applications provided by financial-sector regulators or institutions such as CCIL, NSE and BSE; platforms such as Reuters, Bloomberg and SWIFT; off-the-shelf products with no or minimal customisation; services obtained as a sub-member of a Centralised Payment System from another RE; and Business Correspondent services, payroll processing and statement printing. Paragraph 58(3) further excludes, as service providers, vendors providing business services using IT (such as BCs), RBI-authorised Payment System Operators, partnership-based FinTechs offering co-branded products (handled under Chapter III), FinTechs providing data retrieval, validation and verification, telecom providers of leased lines, and security or audit consultants acting as independent auditors; an RE providing an IT service can itself be a service provider.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx maps services[].type in company-profile/<c>/vendors/<vendor_id>.json (cloud-iaas, cloud-paas, cloud-saas, data-centre, network, security-operations, software-development, managed-service) to the in-scope list and records the exclusion relied on for anything left out. An exclusion that does not match the listed categories is a finding against 58(2). Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 5; UCB 5; LAB/AIFI/CIC 4-5; no equivalent paragraph in the RCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Service-by-service scope classification with the exclusion relied on

groups.title: Chapter II - Role of the Board

controls.title: Outsourcing does not diminish the obligations of the entity, its Board and Senior Management
controls.prose: Outsourcing of any activity does not diminish the obligations of the regulated entity or of its Board and Senior Management, who retain the ultimate responsibility for the outsourced activity.
controls.guidance: Evidence named accountable owners for every material arrangement in company-profile/<c>/vendors/<vendor_id>.json and Board or committee minutes that show oversight. Contract language shifting regulatory accountability to the vendor is a finding. UCB and RCB texts name the MD / CEO with Senior Management. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 9; UCB 9; RCB 8; LAB/AIFI/CIC 8.
controls.category: Chapter II - Role of the Board
evidenceExpected: Accountable owner per material outsourcing arrangement
Board or committee oversight minutes

controls.title: Board-approved outsourcing policies for financial and IT outsourcing
controls.prose: An entity intending to outsource any financial or IT activity must put in place a corresponding comprehensive Board-approved outsourcing policy, with the coverage set out in paragraph 20 (financial services) and paragraph 62 (IT services).
controls.guidance: Obtain each policy and the approving Board minute. The Directions set no review frequency; Maxwell treats a policy not re-approved within 12 months (or its own stated cycle) as a medium finding and a missing policy as high. LAB, AIFI and CIC Directions require only the IT outsourcing policy; the RCB Directions only the financial-services policy. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 10; UCB 10; RCB 9; LAB/AIFI/CIC 9.
controls.category: Chapter II - Role of the Board
evidenceExpected: Board-approved financial services outsourcing policy
Board-approved IT outsourcing policy
Board minutes approving each policy

controls.title: Board framework to evaluate risk and materiality, approval authorities and regular review
controls.prose: The Board, or a Board committee to which powers are delegated, is responsible for a framework to evaluate the risks and materiality of all existing and prospective outsourcing arrangements, for laying down approval authorities by risk and materiality, and for regular review.
controls.guidance: Evidence the approved materiality framework, the delegation-of-authority matrix and the most recent Board or committee review of the arrangements. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 11; UCB 11; RCB 10; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
controls.category: Chapter II - Role of the Board
evidenceExpected: Materiality and risk evaluation framework
Approval authority matrix
Minutes of the latest Board or committee review

controls.title: Board duties for financial-services outsourcing
controls.prose: For outsourcing of financial services the Board, or a committee to which powers are delegated, is responsible for approving the framework to evaluate risks and materiality of all existing and prospective arrangements and the policies that apply to them; laying down approval authorities by risk and materiality; setting up a suitable administrative framework of Senior Management; regularly reviewing outsourcing strategies and arrangements for continued relevance, safety and soundness; and deciding which business activities of a material nature are outsourced and approving those arrangements.
controls.guidance: Evidence each duty in Board or committee minutes. The UCB (12) and RCB (10) texts also require the Board to assess management competencies to develop outsourcing risk policies and to ensure a robust internal audit system over outsourced financial activities. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 12; UCB 12; RCB 10; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
controls.category: Chapter II - Role of the Board
evidenceExpected: Board or committee minutes approving the framework and material arrangements
Record of the latest strategy review

controls.title: NBFCs: Board approves the policy for outsourcing financial services to group entities
controls.prose: For an NBFC, the Board or a delegated committee approves a policy for outsourcing financial services to a group entity.
controls.guidance: Obtain the group-outsourcing policy and approval minute; cross-check vendors with intraGroup true in company-profile/<c>/vendors/<vendor_id>.json. NBFC Directions only; the bank Directions carry no equivalent Board duty.
controls.category: Chapter II - Role of the Board
evidenceExpected: Board-approved policy on outsourcing financial services to group entities

controls.title: Board reviews records of all material outsourcing half-yearly
controls.prose: The Board reviews the records of all material outsourcing on a half-yearly basis; where an NBFC delegates this review, the delegation may be only to the Risk Management Committee.
controls.guidance: Obtain the last two half-yearly review minutes and the central record reviewed (paragraph 36). A gap longer than six months is a high finding; an NBFC delegation to any committee other than the RMC is a medium finding. CB/SFB/PB 12(1)(v); UCB 12(vii); RCB 10(vii) (half-yearly, without the RMC-only delegation limit).
controls.category: Chapter II - Role of the Board
evidenceExpected: Half-yearly Board or RMC minutes reviewing the material outsourcing record

params.label: Board reviews of the records of all material outsourcing per year

controls.title: Banks: Annual Compliance Certificate on financial-services outsourcing
controls.prose: The Board ensures submission of an Annual Compliance Certificate giving the particulars of contracts for outsourcing of financial services, the prescribed periodicity of audit by internal or external auditors, the major findings of the audit and the action taken: to the Department of Supervision, RBI (Commercial Banks, SFBs, Payments Banks), to the Regional Office of RBI (UCBs) or to NABARD (RCBs).
controls.guidance: Obtain the latest certificate and its submission acknowledgement; compare the contract list with the Chapter III vendors in company-profile/<c>/vendors/. A missing certificate for the last year is a high finding. CB, SFB and PB Directions 12(1)(vi); UCB 12(ix); RCB 10(ix); no equivalent in the NBFC Directions.
controls.category: Chapter II - Role of the Board
evidenceExpected: Annual Compliance Certificate as submitted
Submission acknowledgement

params.label: Annual Compliance Certificates on financial-services outsourcing per year

controls.title: Audit Committee monitors internal audit of outsourced activities and vendor reconciliation ageing
controls.prose: The Audit Committee of the Board monitors the system of internal audit of all outsourced activities, and reviews the ageing analysis of entries pending reconciliation with outsourced vendors and makes efforts to reduce old outstanding items at the earliest.
controls.guidance: Obtain ACB minutes covering the internal audit of outsourced activities and the reconciliation ageing report. The Directions state no frequency; Maxwell re-evidences annually. The UCB (12(viii)) and RCB (10(viii)) texts place the internal audit duty on the Board and have no reconciliation-ageing clause. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 12; UCB 12; RCB 10; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
controls.category: Chapter II - Role of the Board
evidenceExpected: ACB minutes on internal audit of outsourced activities
Ageing analysis of vendor reconciliation items

controls.title: Board duties for IT-services outsourcing
controls.prose: For outsourcing of IT services the Board is responsible for a framework for approval of outsourcing activities by risk and materiality, approving policies to evaluate the risks and materiality of all existing and prospective arrangements, and setting up a suitable administrative framework of Senior Management.
controls.guidance: Evidence the Board approval of the IT outsourcing approval framework and materiality policy. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 13; UCB 13; LAB/AIFI/CIC 10; no equivalent paragraph in the RCB Directions.
controls.category: Chapter II - Role of the Board
evidenceExpected: Board-approved IT outsourcing approval framework and materiality policy

controls.title: Board ensures no conflict of interest in third-party engagements, especially on ownership exceptions
controls.prose: The Board, itself or through a committee, ensures that no conflict of interest arises from third-party engagements, especially when permitting an exception to the rule that a service provider (if not a group company) is not owned or controlled by a director, key managerial personnel, the approver of the arrangement or their relatives (proviso to paragraph 59).
controls.guidance: Obtain related-party declarations for material IT vendors and the Board or committee approval, disclosure and monitoring record for every exception. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 13; UCB 13; LAB/AIFI/CIC 10; no equivalent paragraph in the RCB Directions.
controls.category: Chapter II - Role of the Board
evidenceExpected: Related-party and conflict declarations for IT service providers
Board approvals of ownership exceptions

controls.title: Board reviews adverse developments reported from monitoring of IT outsourcing
controls.prose: The Board reviews any adverse development mentioned in the reports put up to Senior Management on the monitoring and control of outsourced IT activities.
controls.guidance: Obtain the Board papers in which adverse monitoring outcomes (for example SLA breaches, assurance exceptions, incidents at a provider) were tabled, and trace open high findings on vendors to them. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 13; UCB 13; LAB/AIFI/CIC 10; no equivalent paragraph in the RCB Directions.
controls.category: Chapter II - Role of the Board
evidenceExpected: Board papers on adverse developments in IT outsourcing monitoring

groups.title: Chapter III - Outsourcing of Financial Services: A. Definitions

controls.title: Assess materiality of financial-services outsourcing against the prescribed criteria
controls.prose: Material outsourcing means arrangements which, if disrupted, could significantly impact business operations, reputation, profitability or customer service. Materiality is based on the importance of the activity and the significance of its risk; the potential impact on earnings, solvency, liquidity, funding, capital and risk profile; the likely impact on reputation, brand value and ability to meet business objectives if the provider fails; the cost of the outsourcing as a proportion of total operating costs; the aggregate exposure to the same provider across functions; and the significance of the outsourced activity for customer service and protection.
controls.guidance: Record the assessment per arrangement in company-profile/<c>/vendors/<vendor_id>.json (materiality, services[].criticality) with the criteria scored. The CB, SFB and PB texts list five criteria and omit the customer-service criterion; the UCB (14) and RCB (6(2)) texts list all six. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 14; UCB 14; RCB 6(2); no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Materiality assessment per financial-services arrangement with criteria applied

groups.title: Chapter III - Outsourcing of Financial Services: B. Activities that shall not be outsourced

controls.title: Do not outsource core management and decision-making functions
controls.prose: An entity that outsources financial services must not outsource core management functions, including internal audit, strategic and compliance functions, and decision-making functions such as determining compliance with KYC norms for opening deposit accounts, sanction of loans (including retail loans) and management of the investment portfolio. An NBFC in a group or conglomerate may outsource these functions within the group subject to paragraphs 45 to 51. Internal auditors may be on contract although the internal audit function itself remains a management process.
controls.guidance: Review vendor services and application ownership for any provider (including lending service providers and AI or scoring vendors) that takes the KYC-compliance, credit-sanction, compliance, internal-audit or investment-portfolio decision rather than supporting it; refresh-apps flags applications where the decision step runs in a vendor-operated system. The CB and SFB texts (15) omit the strategic function and the group proviso; the PB text (15) omits loan sanction. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 15; UCB 15; RCB 11; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
controls.category: B. Activities that shall not be outsourced
evidenceExpected: Mapping of outsourced services to decision rights
Evidence that sanction, KYC and compliance decisions are taken by the entity

controls.title: UCBs and RCBs: functions that must not be outsourced and conditions for contract audit experts
controls.prose: A UCB (and an RCB, paragraph 11) must not outsource core management functions including policy formulation, internal audit and compliance, compliance with KYC norms, credit sanction and management of the investment portfolio. Experts, including former employees, may be hired on contract for internal audit only if the Audit Committee or Board is assured that the expertise does not exist within the audit function, any conflict of interest is recognised and addressed, and ownership of audit reports rests with regular internal audit functionaries.
controls.guidance: Obtain the list of contract internal auditors with the ACB or Board assurance, conflict assessment and report sign-off by regular staff. UCB Directions para 15; RCB Directions para 11.
controls.category: B. Activities that shall not be outsourced
evidenceExpected: Decision-rights mapping for outsourced services
ACB or Board assurance and conflict assessment for contract audit experts

groups.title: Chapter III - Outsourcing of Financial Services: C. Authorisation, Accountability, and Oversight

controls.title: No prior RBI approval, but arrangements are subject to RBI monitoring and inspection
controls.prose: An entity outsourcing financial services does not require prior RBI approval, but such arrangements are subject to on-site and off-site monitoring and inspection or scrutiny by RBI.
controls.guidance: Informational: keep arrangement records inspection-ready. The CB, SFB and PB texts state no prior approval is needed whether the provider is in or outside India; the RCB text names RBI / NABARD. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 16; UCB 16; RCB 12; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Inspection-ready arrangement records

controls.title: Entity is responsible for its service providers, including DSAs, DMAs and recovery agents
controls.prose: Outsourcing does not diminish the entity obligations to its customers and RBI. The entity is responsible for the actions of its service providers, including Direct Sales Agents, Direct Marketing Agents and recovery agents, and for the confidentiality of customer information available with the service provider, and retains ultimate control of the outsourced activity.
controls.guidance: Evidence agent codes of conduct, conduct monitoring and complaint trending for DSA, DMA and recovery-agent vendors. The UCB (17) and RCB (13) texts name Business Correspondents and their retail outlets or sub-agents instead. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 17; UCB 17; RCB 13; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Conduct monitoring of agents acting for the entity
Customer complaint trend per agent vendor

controls.title: Outsourcing respects law, supervision, oversight, internal control and standard of care
controls.prose: The entity ensures that (i) all relevant laws, regulations, rules, guidelines and conditions of approval, licensing or registration are considered in due diligence; (ii) outsourcing, whether the provider is in India or abroad, does not impede RBI supervision or diminish the entity ability to meet its obligations to the regulator; (iii) it does not impede the entity ability to oversee and manage its activities; (iv) it does not compromise or weaken internal control, business conduct or reputation; and (v) the provider applies the same high standard of care as the entity would if the activity were not outsourced. Paragraph 59 applies (i) to (v) to IT outsourcing.
controls.guidance: Evidence a legal and regulatory checklist in each due-diligence file, supervisory-access terms in contracts, and quality-of-service evidence. Findings cite this id with the sub-clause in the description. The LAB, AIFI and CIC texts list the same conditions in a different order in para 12(i)-(v). Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 18; UCB 18; RCB 14; LAB/AIFI/CIC 12.
evidenceExpected: Legal and regulatory checklist in due-diligence files
Contract terms preserving RBI supervision and entity oversight

controls.title: Financial-services providers not owned or controlled by a director or their relatives
controls.prose: A service provider that is not a group company must not be owned or controlled by any director of the entity or their relatives (as defined under the Companies Act, 2013).
controls.guidance: Obtain director and relative interest declarations and match them against vendor ownership (legalName, ultimateParent in company-profile/<c>/vendors/<vendor_id>.json). Chapter IV (paragraph 59) extends the rule to key managerial personnel and approvers and allows a Board-approved exception. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 18; UCB 18; RCB 14; LAB/AIFI/CIC 12.
evidenceExpected: Director interest declarations matched to vendor ownership

controls.title: Entity files CTRs and STRs for customer activity carried out by service providers
controls.prose: The entity is responsible for making Currency Transaction Reports and Suspicious Transaction Reports to FIU-IND or any other competent authority for customer-related activities carried out by its service providers.
controls.guidance: Trace a sample of provider-originated customer transactions into the AML monitoring and CTR/STR filing process. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 19; UCB 19; RCB 15; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
evidenceExpected: AML monitoring coverage of provider-originated activity
CTR and STR filing records

groups.title: Chapter III - Outsourcing of Financial Services: D. Governance Framework

controls.title: Board-approved financial-services outsourcing policy with the prescribed content
controls.prose: An entity intending to outsource financial services must have a comprehensive Board-approved outsourcing policy that incorporates, among other things, the criteria for selecting activities and service providers, delegation of authority by risk and materiality, and systems to monitor and review the activities.
controls.guidance: Trace each element into the policy. The CB, SFB, PB, UCB (20) and RCB (16) texts also require parameters for defining material outsourcing based on the paragraph 14 criteria. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 20; UCB 20; RCB 16; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Board-approved financial services outsourcing policy
Policy-to-clause trace for paragraph 20

controls.title: Senior Management evaluates, implements, reviews and reports financial-services outsourcing risk
controls.prose: Senior Management is responsible for evaluating the risks and materiality of all existing and prospective outsourcing under the Board-approved framework; developing and implementing sound outsourcing policies and procedures commensurate with the nature, scope and complexity of the outsourcing; periodically reviewing their effectiveness; communicating material outsourcing risks to the Board in a timely manner; and periodically reviewing arrangements to identify new material outsourcing risks.
controls.guidance: Evidence procedures, the latest effectiveness review and risk reports to the Board. The UCB (21) and RCB (17) texts assign these duties to the MD / CEO with Senior Management. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 21; UCB 21; RCB 17; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Outsourcing procedures
Periodic effectiveness review
Material outsourcing risk reports to the Board

controls.title: Contingency plans for outsourced financial services are in place and tested
controls.prose: Senior Management ensures that contingency plans based on realistic and probable disruptive scenarios are in place and tested.
controls.guidance: Obtain contingency plans for each material arrangement and the latest test report; an untested plan is a medium finding. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 21; UCB 21; RCB 17; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Scenario-based contingency plan per material arrangement
Latest contingency test report

controls.title: Independent review and audit of compliance with outsourcing policies
controls.prose: Senior Management ensures independent review and audit for compliance with the set outsourcing policies.
controls.guidance: Obtain the latest internal or external audit report on outsourcing policy compliance and the closure status of its observations. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 21; UCB 21; RCB 17; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Independent audit report on outsourcing policy compliance

groups.title: Chapter III - Outsourcing of Financial Services: E. Risk Management

controls.title: Evaluate and guard against the ten key outsourcing risks
controls.prose: Before entering an outsourcing arrangement the entity evaluates and guards against strategic, reputation, compliance, operational, legal, exit strategy, counterparty, country, contractual, and concentration and systemic risk (including the lack of control over a provider on which the industry has considerable exposure).
controls.guidance: Each risk assessment file in the vendor due-diligence pack should address all ten risk types; a missing risk type for a material arrangement is a medium finding. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 22; UCB 22; RCB 18; no equivalent paragraph in the LAB/AIFI/CIC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Risk assessment per arrangement covering the ten risk types

controls.title: Seek to ensure confidentiality and security of customer information held by providers
controls.prose: The entity seeks to ensure the confidentiality, security, preservation and protection of customer information in the custody or possession of the service provider.
controls.guidance: Probe provider-held customer data stores where access permits (encryption at rest, access logging) and check assurance[] reports for confidentiality exceptions. Equivalent paragraphs in the sibling entity-wise Directions (located by comparing the nine RBI texts): CB/SFB/PB 23; UCB 23; RCB 19; LAB/AIFI/CIC 23.
evidenceExpected: Data protection controls for customer data at providers
Assurance report exceptions and remediation

controls.title: Provider access to customer information on a need-to-know basis

groups.title: Chapter III - Outsourcing of Financial Services: F.1 Service Provider Evaluation

controls.prose: The entity performs appropriate due diligence while considering or renewing an outsourcing arrangement, to assess the provider capability to comply with the obligations in the outsourcing agreement on an ongoing basis.
